elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 22.1: "Vendor may audit Customer not more than once per 12 months" — replaces the original "at any time without notice".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 22.1: "an independent auditor bound by confidentiality obligations".

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained § 22.2: "Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall."

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: Retained § 22.2: "Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly..."; the conflicting remote-access grant in § 22.1 ("may remotely access Customer's systems") has been deleted, removing the internal contradiction.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 22.1 caps audits at "not more than once per 12 months", which is a once-per-year limit.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 22.1 gives 30 days' written notice, which exceeds the 15-day fallback minimum.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained § 22.2 flips costs to Customer at an underpayment "exceeding five percent", not ten percent; read literally the fallback threshold is not present. This is immaterial because the preferred 5% element is the operative checklist item and the preferred level is complete.

reasons: All eight preferred elements are met in operative language: § 22.1 as rendered supplies frequency (once per 12 months), 30 days' written notice, business hours, off-site where possible, and an independent auditor bound by confidentiality; § 22.2 already supplies the 5% cost-shift threshold and the express no-direct-access bar, and both were retained verbatim.

The walk-away features of the original § 22.1 (unlimited, unannounced audits and remote system access) are removed, and the contradiction with § 22.2's no-direct-access sentence is resolved rather than left dangling.

Minimality holds: the edit replaces only the single offending sentence in § 22.1, which had to be rewritten in full because every one of its terms (timing, notice, remote access) was non-compliant; no survival tails, procedures, expense allocations, or other extras were added, and the Customer-favourable § 22.2 carve-outs (Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, another supplier's confidential information) were left untouched.

Intent is preserved: Vendor retains a usage-verification right, the cost-shift and shortfall-payment mechanic in § 22.2 continues to operate against the audit right in § 22.1, and no cross-reference or defined term is left undefined.

Fallback level is not independently complete only because the retained cost trigger sits at five percent rather than ten percent; no repair is required since the position is complete at the preferred level.
